title: The Bloody Code: Crime in England, 1660-1800
description: Crime, society and the administration of criminal justice in early modern England. Themes include the political and social backdrop to the "Bloody Code" and contemporary views of criminality, gender and class. Charts the emergence of modern criminal administration - policing, prosecution, trial and punishment - with particular attention to the interrelationship between the law and its social context.
notes: Credit will be granted for only one of HSTR 318, HIST 330, HIST 339 (if taken as section F01 of Sep-Dec 2005).
